Keeping peptides cool in Queen Creek

This page uses NOAA's 1991 to 2020 normals for the Chandler Heights station, about 4.6 miles west-southwest of Queen Creek's Census center point.52 The normals there rest on 14 years of station records.5 July averages a high of 104.2 °F and a low of 78.5 °F, and January a high of 65.6 °F and a low of 40.7 °F.5 The station averages 94.8 days a year at or above 100 °F, against 111.3 at Phoenix Sky Harbor, and 165.4 days at or above 90 °F.68 Its July nights run 6 °F cooler than the airport's 84.5 °F.57 Winter brings 10.5 nights a year at or below 32 °F.6

Summer is still the season to bring a parcel indoors quickly. Freezing nights matter less to a freeze-dried vial than they might seem, because peptide makers recommend freezer storage for the long term anyway: below -15 °C (5 °F) in Bachem's guidance and -20 °C (-4 °F) in GenScript's.910 What they warn against is cycling. GenScript says peptides put through freeze-thaw cycles are susceptible to degradation, and it recommends splitting a peptide into single-use aliquots so the stock is thawed, and opened, less often.10

Once a peptide is dissolved, research guidance and drug labels part ways. Bachem advises against storing peptides in solution for long. For any storage, it says to split the solution into aliquots kept frozen below -15 °C, and that frozen solutions may last a few weeks.9 Labels for approved freeze-dried medicines say the opposite about their own mixed solutions: EGRIFTA SV and ZOMACTON both say not to freeze after mixing.1112 The rule that counts is the one for the product in hand. The storage guide and the reconstitution guide cover the general steps.

About Queen Creek

The Town of Queen Creek incorporated on September 5, 1989.13 Its founding families came in the early 1900s, when the area was called Rittenhouse, to farm cotton, corn and potatoes.13 The town takes its name from Queen Creek, a creek once called Picket Post Creek that was renamed when the Silver Queen Mine opened.13

The town reports just over 2,500 residents in 1990, soon after it incorporated.13 The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 89,770, up 8.2 percent in one year from 82,973.1 Maricopa County as a whole grew about 6 percent over the five years from April 2020.1

Queen Creek covers 42.08 square miles of land.2 San Tan Mountain Regional Park, a Maricopa County park with a Queen Creek mailing address, spans more than 10,000 acres of lower Sonoran Desert, and its elevation runs from roughly 1,400 feet to more than 2,500 feet.14 The town's own Horseshoe Park and Equestrian Centre covers 38 acres on Riggs Road, west of Ellsworth Road, and hosts English and Western horse shows, vendor fairs, concerts and rodeos.15

The town is young and family-heavy. In the 2024 American Community Survey, its median age was 33.4, a third of residents (33.9 percent) were under 18, and 10.1 percent were 65 or older.1617 Owner-occupied homes make up 88.0 percent of occupied housing, and workers average a 32.2-minute trip to work.181917 The governor's office lists LG Energy Solution's battery gigafactory in Queen Creek as North America's largest standalone battery project.20

Banner Ironwood Medical Center, a nonprofit acute care hospital with emergency services, uses a Queen Creek mailing address but sits in Pinal County, according to federal Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services data.21 The same data list three more acute care hospitals with emergency services in Gilbert: Mercy Gilbert Medical Center, Banner Gateway Medical Center and East Valley ER and Hospital.22

Queen Creek is one of the member governments of the Mesa Gateway Airport Authority, which owns and runs Mesa Gateway Airport. The airport began as Williams Air Force Base, reopened in March 1994 as Williams Gateway Airport, and now offers nonstop flights to more than 40 cities.23

Nearby

Gilbert's Census center point is about 9 miles from Queen Creek's, and Peptides in Gilbert covers that town.2 Mesa and Chandler have pages too. Frequently asked questions

Do you ship to the Pinal County part of Queen Creek?

Yes. The town straddles two counties: of its 89,770 residents in the July 2025 estimates, 74,563 lived in the Maricopa County part and 15,207 in the Pinal County part.1 Orders to either side ship from the USA and Canada under the same shipping policy. Even the town's main ZIP Code Tabulation Area, 85142, crosses the line, with only about 32 percent of its land in Maricopa County.4

Is there a D2C Peptides location in Queen Creek?

Not at this time. D2C Peptides has no storefront, office or address in Queen Creek, which is why no street address, phone number or map appears here. Queen Creek is served by shipping, and order questions go through the contact page. The locations page lists the other places with pages.

Can Queen Creek buyers check lab documents before ordering?

Start with the lab results page, where D2C Peptides posts certificates of analysis as they become available. If the document you need for a particular product or lot is not there, ask through the contact page before you order. What happens if a parcel arrives damaged is set out on the returns page.
